title: Early Indian Palmistry: Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna: Pāṇilekhā
author: Kenneth G. Zysk

dates.original_text_composition: c. 1st–2nd century CE (narrative frame of Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna / Divyāvadāna corpus)
dates.redaction_date: After 864 CE (latter half of 9th century CE; incorporation of Pāṇilekhā and divination chapters)
dates.manuscript_witness: 11th–19th century Nepalese Sanskrit palm-leaf & paper manuscripts (e.g. Cambridge Add. 865, Asiatic Society of Bengal, National Archives of Nepal)
dates.earlier_scholarly_research: Zysk, The Indian System of Human Marks (2 vols., Brill, 2016)
dates.first_printed_edition: 1954 (Sujitkumar Mukhopadhyaya ed., The Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna, Visvabharati, Santiniketan, pp. 64–66)
dates.critical_edition_or_translation: Kenneth G. Zysk (Critical Sanskrit edition, English translation, and philological analysis)

edition: History of Science in South Asia (HSSA), Volume 13 (2025), pp. 240–275; ISSN 2369-7725
language: Sanskrit (with English translation and critical apparatus)

rights.rights_basis: Published open access in History of Science in South Asia under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Underlying ancient Sanskrit text is public domain worldwide.
rights.notes: Published under CC BY 4.0 license permitting commercial and non-commercial adaptation with attribution. Underlying Sanskrit verse fragments are public domain.

notes: The authoritative scholarly critical edition and translation of the 34 Pāṇilekhā verses from the Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna. Documents the integration of astral science (jyotiḥśāstra) into Buddhist palmistry.

title: Bṛhat Saṃhitā
author: Varāhamihira

dates.manuscript_witness: Multiple Sanskrit manuscripts throughout Indian subcontinent
dates.critical_edition_or_translation: 1981 (English translation by M. Ramakrishna Bhat, Motilal Banarsidass)

rights.rights_basis: The original 6th-century Sanskrit root text is in the public domain worldwide. Later 20th-century translations (such as M.R. Bhat 1981) remain under copyright in India and international jurisdictions.
rights.notes: All rule definitions cite the public domain Sanskrit verse contents and independent Kai RegAI English translations. No proprietary modern commentary text is reproduced.

notes: Encyclopedic Sanskrit treatise covering physical palm contours, finger proportions, and royal bodily marks (Maha-Lakshanas).

title: Hastasañjīvana
author: Meghavijaya Gaṇi

dates.manuscript_witness: Western Indian Jain library manuscripts (Patan, Ahmedabad)

rights.rights_basis: Authored in 1680 CE; printed editions published prior to 1929 are in the public domain in the US and worldwide under rule of shorter term.
rights.notes: Original manuscript verses and 1928 edition text are in the public domain.

notes: Comprehensive medieval monograph detailing line variations and intersection effects.

title: Practical Palmistry (Hastarekha Vigyan)
author: Dr. Narayan Dutt Shrimali

rights.rights_basis: Protected under the Indian Copyright Act 1957 (life of author + 60 years; author deceased 1998, protected through 2058) and the Berne Convention.
rights.notes: Strictly limited to the extraction of uncopyrightable factual correspondences, feature correlations, and traditional Sanskrit rule conditions. Verbatim prose replication is prohibited.

notes: Influential 20th-century Indian work adapting classical Samudrika to modern professional careers.

title: The Laws of Scientific Hand Reading: A Practical Treatise on the Art Commonly Called Palmistry
author: William G. Benham

dates.first_printed_edition: 1900 / 1901 (G.P. Putnam's Sons, New York and London)

edition: First Edition, G.P. Putnam's Sons, 1901, 635 pp.

rights.rights_basis: Published in the United States in 1901 (prior to January 1, 1929), placing it in the US public domain. In the UK/EU, author William G. Benham passed away in 1944 (1944 + 70 years = entered UK/EU public domain on January 1, 2015).
rights.notes: The 1901 original edition is in the public domain in the US and UK/EU. Later modern editorial introductions or reprints with new content maintain copyright over those additions only.

notes: Historical Western palmistry manual. Note: The word 'Scientific' in the title reflects 1900-era chirognomic terminology and does NOT denote modern empirical scientific validation.

title: Palmistry for All: Containing New Information on the Study of the Hand Never Before Published
author: Cheiro (Count Louis Hamon)

dates.first_printed_edition: 1916 (Herbert Jenkins Ltd., London; G.P. Putnam's Sons, New York)

rights.rights_basis: Published in 1916 (pre-1929 US public domain). In UK/EU, author Louis Hamon died in 1936 (1936 + 70 years = entered UK/EU public domain on January 1, 2007).
rights.notes: The 1916 original print edition is in the public domain in the US and Europe.

notes: Classic historical work on hand types, major lines, and mounts.
